segments.text: You ever wondered what the oldest animal is that we've ever discovered?
Well, if you haven't, you're definitely wondering it now, so let's talk about it.
Maybe it's an elephant.
They live for a long time, right?
Or maybe it's a whale. Those also live for a long time.
Nope, not an elephant or a whale. It's something much, much more exciting.
Are you ready for this?
Behold, the oldest animal ever discovered.
This clam, whose name is Ming.
Ming was dredged up by researchers off the coast of Iceland in 2006.
Now, when they first found him, they just thought Ming was a clam.
You know, they hadn't made an introduction yet.
They brought Ming and a bunch of his buddies back to their lab for study.
Another data point was looking at how old the clams were, which you can actually do fairly easily.
The clam shells are deposited in layers like tree rings.
So if you count the layers, you can figure out how old the clam is.
Fortunately, you can't do this while the clam's alive, so they had to freeze all of them.
And it was only after that that they sampled Ming and learned that it was 507 years old.
It'd be really cool to make a discovery like this,
but it also come with the realization that you just killed the oldest single individual animal on the planet.
